<description>
After #33259, `getblockchaininfo` reports the progress of the background chainstate relative to the snapshot base block, but `getchainstates` still computes `verificationprogress` against the network tip for every chainstate, so the same node reports two different numbers for the same chainstate.

This PR modifies `verificationprogress` value to report the correct value, relative to the block the chainstate actually stops at.
</description>

Concept ACK

I’m currently running a node with AssumeUTXO, so I checked this before and after applying the change. My snapshot base is at height 935000.

Before the fix, at background height 474828, the background chainstate’s `verificationprogress` in `getchainstates` reported 16.73%, while `backgroundvalidation.verificationprogress` in `getblockchaininfo` reported 18.22% for the same block. After the fix, at height 475948, both reported exactly 0.1834620809971763. This is a good improvement: `getchainstates` now reports background progress toward the snapshot base, as `getblockchaininfo` already does.

Locally, the full functional test passed. Reverting only the RPC fix made the background-progress assertion fail; restoring it made the full test pass again.
